{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker

}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker

    | name      = Unknown Speaker

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker

}}

    | name      = Unknown Speaker

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:10.039
    | text      = So Governor Abbott has made some news out of Texas because he has announced that he's kicked a bunch of people off the voter rolls. Great.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:19.039

}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:21.039
    | text      = It's just the level of lying when you think they can't turn up the lies anymore, when the lies backfire on them, when the lies don't work anymore.

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:29.039
    | text      = Their answer is just get even crazier. And they've caught all these millions of illegal aliens signed up and dead people to vote.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:37.039
    | text      = Just in Texas alone, a bunch of other states found the same thing and just expunged them off the rolls.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:42.039
    | text      = And the Democrats are going into total conniption fits, filing lawsuits to keep the illegal aliens and dead people on the voter rolls.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:49.039
    | text      = I mean, you can't make that up. Just in Texas alone, Governor Greg Abbott removes over one million ineligible voters, including nearly 500,000 dead people and illegal aliens.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:17:59.039
    | text      = I mean, wow.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:02.039
    | text      = So recently, Texas Governor Greg Abbott announced that they had removed approximately a million ineligible voters from the Texas rolls.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:09.039
    | text      = In the real world, this is something that happens kind of regularly. Every state has a process in place to routinely trim the rolls.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:17.039
    | text      = But it's obviously not a perfect system. And generally, folks that care about civil liberties agree that it's best to err on the side of not restricting voting access.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:25.039
    | text      = Making sure that everyone's on the roll, who is a fully qualified voter, that's a process that would take an almost comical amount of time and organization.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:33.039
    | text      = And the funding and infrastructure doesn't really exist to handle that on the state level.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:38.039
    | text      = So in the case of Texas, they have processes like sending notices to potentially dead voters or voters who have moved and not updated their registration location.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:47.039
    | text      = It takes multiple times not hearing back to justify kicking someone off the rolls, which is good, but it's also kind of inefficient.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:18:55.039
    | text      = The Democrats aren't suing Abbott. He's being sued by civil liberties groups that argue that his purge of the rolls is illegal because it's unclear what standards his office used to make the cuts,
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:05.039
    | text      = and because it's a federal crime to remove voters from the rolls within 90 days of an election.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:10.039
    | text      = This is a provision that's important because if it weren't there, it would be super easy for a state to widely disenfranchise particular groups of people by erroneously kicking them off voter rolls close to an election so they wouldn't have the time to sort it out before it was time to vote.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:24.039
    | text      = Or more simply, you could just create more administrative hurdles to suppress voter turnout this way.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:30.039
    | text      = For instance, in this case, over 6,500 alleged non-citizens were kicked off the voter rolls, but no basis was given for determining these non-citizens.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:39.039
    | text      = It's very possible that some of these people are people who, like, they have a right to vote and they've been misidentified, so they're having their votes deprived by this. That's very possible.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:51.039
    | text      = Texas did this in 2019 when their secretary of state's office flagged 95,000 registered voters as being ineligible.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:19:58.039
    | text      = As that number was examined closer, it was discovered that these people were almost all mistakenly flagged.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:04.039
    | text      = In one county, the elections administrator had been sent a list of 8,035 people who quote-unquote shouldn't be on the rolls,
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:11.039
    | text      = and the Texas Tribune reported that he ended up finding two non-citizens in the bunch, both of whom marked that they were not citizens on their registrations, but who had accidentally been added to the rolls by the, like, office side of things.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:24.039
    | text      = Sure, sure, sure, sure.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:25.039
    | text      = It was not their fault.

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:32.039

}}

{{TranscriptBlock

    | text      = Because it's illegal.

{{TranscriptBlock

    | text      = ...glaring this was.

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:40.039
    | text      = Yeah, yeah, yeah.
}}

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
    | timestamp = 00:20:41.039
    | text      = This kind of action is generally not motivated by a need to clean up the voter rolls, this kind of push to get people off the voter rolls.

    | text      = Yeah.

{{TranscriptBlock

{{TranscriptBlock
    | name      = Unknown Speaker
